newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl urges Germans to honour legacy of anti-Nazis.
newsitem.headline: Kohl urges Germans to honour legacy of anti-Nazis.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Sunday used the anniversary of a failed assassination attempt on Adolf Hitler to urge Germans to be vigilant against extremism and intolerance.

"Radicals, whether they come from left or right, must not get the chance again to determine the fate of our country," Kohl said in a declaration to recall July 20, 1944, when plotters tried to kill the Nazi leader at his Eastern front headquarters.
"The memory of July 20, 1944 is an impetus and obligation for all democrats in Germany to uphold freedom, the law and peace together," the chancellor said.
Army officer Count Claus Schenk von Stauffenberg carried out the assassination attempt by planting a timebomb in a briefcase at the headquarters in Rastenburg.
The blast wrecked the room, killing four of the men present, but big oak supports under a table shielded the Nazi leader and he escaped with minor injuries.
Unaware his attack had failed, Stauffenberg flew to Berlin to put his plans for a coup into action, but he and other ringleaders were captured by the SS and shot that same night.
Right-wing extremist violence surged after German unfication in 1990 but officials say it has declined in recent years.

Germany's anti-extremist watchdog, the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution, estimates there are 6,000 militant right-wingers prepared to use violence and that they have around 35,000 sympathisers.
